articleTitle: Identification of wireless transceiver devices using radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting based on STFT analysis to enhance authentication security
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Wireless transceiver devices radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting (RFF) distinct native feature is a physical layer based security authentication method that enhances wireless security authentication, which is especially useful for the power and computing limited devices. However, the high authentication rate is necessary for the security purpose. In this paper, we propose a new approach where the radio frequency finger-printing is based on the short time Fourier transform (STFT) analysis. Specifically, in order to identify four wireless transceiver devices of same manufacture and batch, we combine the STFT with the support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. Our simulation results show that the average correct identification probability is higher than 80.5% even when the signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) is 0 dB. It is demonstrated that the novel method has high capability to against the noise.

articleTitle: Motion artifact removal for wearable ECG using stationary wavelet multi-resolution analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) is attracting much attention in daily healthcare applications. From the view-point of long-term use, it is desired that the electrodes are non-contact with the human body. In this study, we propose an algorithm using the stationary wavelet transform (SWT) to remove motion artifact superimposed on ECG signal when using non-contact capacitively coupling electrodes. In addition, we confirmed that the proposed algorithm performed well on the ECG signals including a premature ventricular contraction (PVC) using MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. As a result, the correlation coefficients of ECG signals with respect to the clean ones have been improved from 0.61 to 0.84 on median before and after motion artifact removal, which demonstrates the validity of the proposed SWT-based algorithm.

articleTitle: A study on ESD protection characteristic difference measurement of TVS diodes by VNA
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The protection performance of an electrostatic-discharge (ESD) protection device changes when the device is implemented in a circuit at a system level. Additionally, the operating characteristics and protection performance of an ESD-protection device may differ from device to device even if the specifications of both devices are the same. Therefore, this study aims to realize an evaluation and simulation method that can express realistic differences in the ESD-protection-performance of devices relying on transient voltage suppressor (TVS) diodes. First, we evaluated the resolution of the proposed method for measuring the protection characteristics of TVS diodes using a vector network analyzer. Second, we measured and compared four types of TVS diodes that have very similar specifications. We present the measured results for the frequency responses of the four similar TVS diodes in their operating and non-operating states. In addition, the reproducibility of the TVS-diode measurement for different printed circuit board (PCB) patterns was also examined. The results confirmed that our proposed method can express the differences between the four similar TVS diodes in terms of the attenuation of the pass frequency responses. In addition, the reproducibility of the measurement for different PCB patterns is also confirmed.

articleTitle: Chaos PWM for EMI reduction in a high boost DC-DC converter with coupled inductors
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper a chaotic PWM control for a DC-DC converter with coupled inductors and input zero ripple is presented. The use of a choatic PWM represents one solution adopted to reduce Electromagnetic Emmission at the output of power converters due to their non-liner behaviour. In this work a chaotic PWM has been implemented in Matlab-Simulink envaironment for the DC-DC converter under study and a comparison with a traditional PWM control has been made. A descrition of the method used to generate the chaotic carrier has been presented and the effect on the EMI mitigation, obtained by spreading the energy spectrum of the output voltage, has been shown. Moreover, the benefits of chaotic PWM in terms of the converter efficiency has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: A novel FMCW waveform for multi-target detection and the corresponding algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Frequency Modulation Continuous Wave (FMCW) as a quite practical radar modulation technique, is increasingly applied in the intelligent transportation field. A classical FMCW radar system has good performance of short-range applications. However, in multi-target detection situations, so-called ghost targets usually occur because of the Doppler effect in the echo signal, leading to the false alarm rate. For solving this problem, a novel FMCW waveform is proposed, which consists of two parts: a trapezoid wave and a triangle wave. In accordance to a trapezoid wave, the ambiguous ranges are calculated by the slow ramp and the unambiguous relative velocities are detected by the flat frequencies. Nevertheless, some ghost targets still remain owing to the mismatch of intersections in Velocity-Range (V-R) map. Thus, another triangular pairing algorithm is added. It helps that the rest of ghost targets are completely removed. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed waveform of multiple chirp signals with different slopes behaves well.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic interference of vehicle GPS navigation equipment
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of the automotive industry, a large amount of electronic equipment was installed into the car. Due to the space constraints, lots of complex electromagnetic compatibility problems occur caused by the electromagnetic interference between different instruments. Therefore, for GPS navigation equipment installed inside the vehicle, a good electromagnetic compatibility and anti-jamming performance is significant. This paper describes the electromagnetic interference sources that affects the vehicle GPS navigation equipment, analysis the main interference propagation path, as well as this paper provides some of the optimization method to reduce the electromagnetic compatibility problems that may be encountered in the real work, which is critical for the safety and reliable operation of the GPS navigation equipment.

articleTitle: Lightning susceptibility analysis of cables in a wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This paper examines the electromagnetic interference (EMI) effects related to a wind turbine hit by lightning. Cables located inside the grounded metallic body of a wind turbine are the subject of focus during the numerical analysis process. In order to assess the interference levels on the cables due to a lightning strike on the turbine, the analysis results include transient currents along the various cable shields, cores and bonding wires, as well as the electromagnetic fields inside and outside of wind turbine. The structure of the wind turbine and its grounding system are modeled using conducting wires, solid metallic surfaces and wire-surface junctions. The computations are performed using an efficient Method of Moments (MoM) numerical tool based on surface-wire integral equations for a stratified medium. Numerical results based on the combined surface-wire modeling technique demonstrate clearly that shield cables can provide a good protection against lightning effects.

articleTitle: Spread spectrum in random PWM DC-DC converters by PSO&GA optimized randomness levels
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized spread spectrum Random PWM technique for the reduction of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) in DC-DC converter to improve the Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) of the system. In particular, the Randomized Pulse Position Modulation (RPPM) is considered and a study of the random laws is developed. Different density probability distributions are analyzed and the randomness levels, that characterize each probability distribution, are optimized in order to reduce the Power Spectral Density (PSD) of the DC-DC converter output voltage. Two optimization techniques are used: the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) technique and the Genetic Algorithm (GA). Four probability density distributions are analyzed, Uniform, Normal, Beta and Generalized Extreme Value Distribution (GEV) distributions, and their effectiveness on spreading the PSD is analyzed. Finally, the effects on the reduction of the output EMI of the converter is shown.

articleTitle: A new method for radio wave propagation prediction based on finite integral method and machine learning
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid scheme based on the ray tracing method and machine learning for the field strength prediction is presented. It uses a triangular face as a basic unit to simulate in CST and gets lots of training data. This method can be divided into two main parts - predicting the field strength with machine learning in near field and converting field strength to rays in far field. In contrast to the results of finite integral (FIT), mean relative error of results predicted by the new model is 0.04 in near field and 0.0583 in far field. And in this way, high prediction accuracy is achieved with less computation time. Comparisons of time performance between the new method, FIT and ray tracing method are presented in the last.

articleTitle: A new method using covariance eigenvalues and time window in passive human motion detection based on CSI phases
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of WLAN technology, device-free passive human detection utilizing the existing WLAN infrastructure has attracted the attention of the numerous scholars and holds more potential to ubiquitous smart applications. Despite of the prevalent signal feature Received Signal Strength (RSS), more reliable and robust feature Channel State Information (CSI) in the 802.11n standard has been proposed in recently years. In this paper, we explore to study the sensibility of amplitude and phase to human motion via CSI. We propose a novel eigenvalue based on phases to represent the full CSI information. With the dynamic time window algorithm, we develop CETW (covariance eigenvalues and time window) method to detect human motion. Based on the above research, we design a high precision device-free passive burst human motion detection system (HPMD). As demonstrated in the experiments, our system gained a high detection rate and a low false alarm rate.

articleTitle: Design of miniaturized low-pass filter with improved Koch fractal DGS
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A miniaturized microstrip low-pass filter (LPF) with ultra-wide stopband is proposed, where improved Koch fractal curve defected ground structure (DGS) resonators are implemented in its design. The improved Koch fractal DGS is composed of a specific schematic Π-shaped DGS with improved Koch fractal curve at both terminations. By using this structure, the filter not only supports conventional DGS performances such as a sharp transition to the stop band, but also exhibits an ultrawide stopband compared with traditional dumbbell-shaped DGS (DB-DGS) filters. The filter containing 2 unit cells has a compact size of 36.8×24 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and operates with an insertion loss of less than 1 dB from dc to 2 GHz. From 2.2 GHz to 6.3 GHz, the rejection is better than 40 dB. The proposed asymmetric Koch fractal DGS-LPF is easily integrated into RF/microwave circuitry at a low manufacturing cost, especially for wireless communication.

articleTitle: Single-layer single-patch wideband dual-beam E-shaped patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A wideband single layer single patch E-shaped microstrip antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna has two distinct directional radiation beams off the broadside direction, which are obtained by operating the rectangular patch at the higher order TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode, instead of the fundamental TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode in a conventional microstrip antenna. The wideband performance is achieved by the two slots incorporated in the rectangular patch. Antenna analysis is carried out by the parametric studies to demonstrate how the slots affect the antenna performance. The simulated impedance bandwidth is 0.65GHz(5.23–5.88GHz), or 11.8% centered at 5.5 GHz, which covers the WLAN 5.8 GHz (5.725–5.825 GHz), WIMAX 5.5 GHz (5.25–5.85GHz), and HiperLAN/2 (5.47–5.725 GHz). At the central frequency 5.5 GHz, the simulated radiation pattern in the E-plane indicates the maximal gains for the dual radiation beams are 7.7 dB directed at −41 and 8.2dB directed at 37, respectively.

articleTitle: Identification of conductive leakage signal in power cable based on multi-classification PSO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In order to effectively identify and extract the red signal from the leakage signal in the computer's power line, a method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed to optimize the multi classification support vector machine (SVM). Firstly, the conductive leakage signal is filtered. Then the SVM penalty parameter and kernel parameter are optimized by PSO, the conduction leakage signal is trained and classified. Finally, the classification performance of the un-optimized SVM is compared with PSO-SVM. The result shows that this method has higher classification rate than the grid search method. The classification and recognition rate reaches 87.23%.

articleTitle: New electromagnetic protection devices based on filtering
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Electromagnetic protection technology is an important part of electromagnetic compatibility, including the study of electromagnetic protection materials and the research of electromagnetic protection devices. Absorbing materials and electromagnetic shielding materials are two major electromagnetic protection materials. Electromagnetic protection devices can protect the electronic equipment from electromagnetic pulse by filtering, grounding and shielding. In this paper, two novel electromagnetic protection devices are introduced. One is a double pass frequency selective surface radome, the other is a filter based on the left-right hand transmission line.

articleTitle: Impedance measurement of RFID tag antenna based on different methods
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: RFID tag antennas use balanced feeding structure, which causes great challenge on antenna impedance measurement. Methods for balanced antenna impedance measurement can be divided into three categories: Balun method, imaging theory and S-parameter method. Three types methods are analyzed and compared in this paper. Simulations and experiments are implemented to support the comparison. Through the comparisons, great agreements in impedance value and variation tendency are observed between the simulation and experiment. Moreover, strengths and weaknesses of the three methods also are analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Burnout effects of microwave pulses on the AlGaN/GaN HEMT in an LNA
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The responses when a microwave pulse is injected into an AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) in a low-noise amplifier (LNA) circuit, are analyzed using our independent-developed device-circuit joint simulator. The correctness of our simulator is verified by comparing the results of the DC characteristics for the HEMT and the performances for the LNA constructed by the HEMT, obtained by our simulator and the Advanced Design System (ADS) software. By studying the temperature distribution in the device, it is found that the hot spot which is the most vulnerable place to be burnt out is located at the edge of the gate near the source.

articleTitle: The inductance comparison of transmission line and conventional spiral inductor
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A novel view has been shown to analyze the choice of inductance between transmission lines and conventional spiral inductor. We systematacially compare this three types of components which have the properties of inductance. We analyze size, inductance, Q-factor, and self-resonance frequency(f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SR</sub>) of the three types components. As a result, when compared on the premise of the same inductance, single coil inductor shows best inductor performance but occupies the biggest area. The spiral inductor shows the highest f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SR</sub>. Besides, the transmission line shows great compromise between the spiral and single coil inductor in millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Single radiator four-port MIMO antenna for WLAN and WIMAX applications with high isolation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A single radiator four-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for WLAN and WIMAX applications is presented. The proposed antenna is composed of a single radiating element and a square ring ground. To reduce mutual coupling among antenna ports, the four feeding ports are placed perpendicular to each other in order to mismatch their polarization. By introducing radiation stubs and ground stubs, impedance matching and isolation is improved. The measured results show a −10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth is from 4.5 to 7.0 GHz (covering the 5.2 GHz/5.8 GHz WLAN and the 5.5 GHz WIMAX bands), and the isolation between various ports below −25 dB.

articleTitle: Research on optimizing visual soil resistivity test method based on theoretical algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The soil parameters, which are the inverse data adopting Canadian software CDEGS (also called isometric pole method) of the result of Wenner quadrupole method measurement, and are the computed data based on the Wenner quadrupole method and improved mathematical algorithm, are different from the actual soil condition. For this reason, in two experimental sites with known soil structures, homogeneous and non-homogeneous, the soil resistivity are repeatedly measured by non-isometric methods (also called general method) and Winner Method, and the soil structure model is obtained by the inverse data via CDEGS. The result are to be compared with the data of field geological exploration in the same experimental sites. The experimental results show that in non-homogeneous soil, the soil layer data inverted by non-isometric methods and symmetrical non-equidistant quadrupole method (also called Bamor method) which is suitable for measurement are more elaborately characterized, and are more corresponding to the data of field geological exploration. The author suggests the standard of soil resistivity measuring method be revised. In addition, in the mathematical model calculation of large projects and the soil with higher grounding requirements, we should determine the convergence and accuracy of the results by the preceding two measuring method rather than totally rely on the improvement of mathematical algorithm.

articleTitle: Information leakage of electromagnetic emission from differential transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, information leakage from electromagnetic radiation of differential transmission lines is analyzed. The model of differential transmission lines is built. And common mode noise caused by unbalance structure of the differential transmission lines and delay between differential drivers is simulated. These common mode noises have a corresponding relationship with the information transmitted over the differential lines. It can cause information leakage. Finally, the experiment presents the possibility of information leakage from differential transmission lines.

articleTitle: A low-profile dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna with metamaterial loading and anti-interference capability
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A novel low-profile and wideband dual-polarized magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is presented for base-station application. The proposed antenna is excited by two orthogonal Γ-shaped probes, which can aslo improve its isolation. The isolation between the two ports is better than 30 dB over the operating frequency. By employing the metamaterial loadings which are fully arranging inside the magnetic dipole, the height of the proposed antennna can be decreased from 28 to 20 mm. Due to the specially designed notches etched in the radiated dipoles, an impedance bandwidth of 69.2% ranging from 1.71 to 3.60 GHz, together with a notch-band frequency bandwidth ranging from 2.35 to 2.55 GHz can be achieved.

articleTitle: A non-terminal points grounding method of shielded cable for electromagnetic pulse protection
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A novel non-terminal points grounding method is proposed to improve shielding effectiveness of shielded cables for electromagnetic pulse protection. Compared with traditional method, grounding locations of proposed method are modified by current distribution on cable sheath, rather than two endpoints of cable. Shielding effect in terms of core currents are analyzed in detail. Factors including incident angle and cable length are also considered to verify effectiveness of the proposed method Simulation results show that there exists best grounding location. The coupled electromagnetic energy of shielded cable could reduce 92.7% compared to the traditional one's, on the best grounding location in case of 1m cable under irradation of High-altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP).

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of electromagnetic disturbance at the secondary side of electronic voltage transformer due to switching operations via a 6 kv switchgear
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, the transient disturbance voltage induced at the secondary side of the electronic voltage transformer are measured when the circuit breaker of a 6kV switchgear are open/closed. The typical characteristics of the measured voltage waveform are analyzed. The results show that the waveform looks like a damped oscillatory wave with peak voltage up to 50.62V, the rise time about 8∼16ns, and the dominant frequencies between 1–60MHz. These results are helpful for establishing the immunity test standard waveform for secondary equipment deployed around the switchgear.

articleTitle: A sharp-rejection dual-bandstop filter with multiple transmission poles and zeros based on transversal signal-interaction concepts
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A new sharp-rejection dual-bandstop filter is proposed in this paper. Two wide stopbands are realized by Path 1 composed of a T-type structure. Three transmission poles in each stop-band and nine transmission zeros out of band within 2f0 are achieved by the signal interaction of Path 1 and Path 2, guaranteeing sharp rejection and high filtering performance. In addition, the extraction process of the transmission poles and zeros is presented based on S-parameters theory. The 3-dB fractional bandwidths of 67.8% and 33.0% with the center frequency 0.575 and 1.425 GHz are obtained. The measured results agrees well with those of simulation.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of IoT system and equipment for lightning parameter monitoring
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Lightning is a familiar natural phenomenon, which is heard sometimes that thunder causes damages to the electrical appliances and facilities. So the lightning protection device has been a necessity to make sure the security of production and living. Earthing is a very important part of a lightning protection system. We propose a earthing method that solves the problem of high cost of the traditional method, design and realize an Internet-of-Things (IoT) system for lightning parameter monitoring. The nodes of wireless sensor network (WSN) measure the value of grounding resistance and many other operation parameters. The operation parameters data is reported and send to the data server through the wireless gateway. All the real-time data is processed and showed by the server through a lightning parameter monitoring software. The hardware of IoT node used in the lightning parameter monitoring system and sensing the parameters successfully. Experiment is carried out and the result shows that the system is effective.

articleTitle: TEMPEST in USB
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of the computer data cable (USB cable) electromagnetic leakage, we can first use the near field coupling coil to collect the leaked electromagnetic signals, and meanwhile use oscilloscope to save the signals. After that, we will use the ESN (echo state network) to extract the characteristics of the collected electromagnetic signals and then use the SVM (support vector machine) method to pattern identify the characteristics of signals. This article mainly introduce an experiment, which divides 0-9(ten numbers) into 5 groups according to the difference of ASCLL code in Hamming weigh and then identify these 5 groups separately.

articleTitle: Simulation research on the return conductor configuration for lightning indirect effect test of metal cylinder
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, a method for constructing the experimental device for lightning indirect effect of the metal cylinder flying object is studied, and a cage-like frame similar to coaxial line is designed as the coupling device. Through the electromagnetic simulation software CST, the influence of the different load impedance and the different return conductor structures on the simulation results is obtained. The current resonance of system is analyzed by observing the current waveform of load which has different values. By calculating the surface current of metal cylinder, the impact of return conductor arrangement on the metal cylinder surface current distribution uniformity is analyzed. Finally, it is concluded that the system does not produce resonance in the case of different load impedances. When the system length is small, the size of the load impedance can be selected flexibly according to the actual experiment needs. The larger the number of return conductors and the smaller the distance between the conductor and the metal cylinder are, the more uniform the current distribution is. The simulation results provide foundation for the actual experiment.

articleTitle: A high gain LTCC ring-loaded patch antenna array at 140 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A 4×4 low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) antenna array working at 140ghz is proposed, with a high gain of 19.2 dBi at 140 GHz and a bandwidth of 8.7 GHz from 136.9 GHz to 145.6 GHz for S11 less than -10dB, which has a small antenna dimension of 6.5×12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna element is a ring-loaded patch antenna with a SIW cavity backed. It can achieve a high gain of 9.5 dBi at 140 GHz. A substrate integrated wave-guide (SIW) power-divider and a transition from SIW to waveport are designed to form the 4×4 array.

articleTitle: 3D flexible multi-probe setups for MIMO OTA testing
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This paper presents a method to construct 3D flexible multi-probe setups for MIMO OTA testing. The optimal OTA probe locations are determined on the surface of a whole sphere in 3D flexible multi-probe setups proposed. The proposed method applies both genetic algorithm and convex optimization to 3D flexible multi-probe setups, which obtains better emulation accuracy of the 3D channel spatial correlation at the receiver side. Simulation results show that the proposed 3D flexible multi-probe setups with a smaller number of OTA probes can achieve more accurate 3D spatial correlation accuracy within the test volume for MIMO OTA testing.

articleTitle: The comparison of frequency domain method and time domain method in absorber reflectivity measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, it is presented that the reflectivity measurement comparison of the same absorber sample in frequency domain method and time domain method. In the frequency domain measurement, the arch method is used to measure the reflection signal of absorber sample and metal plate with the same dimension. The time-gate function of a Vector Network Analyzer(VNA) is needed for data processing. In the time domain measurement, a short pulse signal is used to separate the absorber reflection signal in accordance with the different arrival time. A reference reflection signal measurement method is proposed according to the principle of specular reflection other than metal plate reflection in this paper. Based on the measurement results comparison of the same sample in both methods, it can be seen that this time domain measurement method is feasible. However, it still needs be studied further in the future research.

articleTitle: Interference mechanism of high repetitive frequency UWS-EMP to communication receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The interference experiment of a communication receiver by ultra-wide spectrum electromagnetic pulse (UWS-EMP) is carried out and the interference process is monitored based on the design of experimental approach and experimental system. The research shows that the interference to High-speed Frequency Hopping communication, Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) communication and Fixed Frequency communication by UWS-EMP is effective. Combined with the non-linear responses of key communication devices caused by UWS-EMP, the interference mechanism is presented as follows: the intense UWS-EMP in ns order passing through the low noise amplifier (LNA), mixer and filter of receiver is converted to the secondary interference signal with largely extended duration, then the automatic gain control (AGC) circuit is disturbed by the secondary interference signal and the AGC control voltage is turned to be abnormal, therefore, the gain of the receiver is declined, the normal signal can't be amplified sufficiently and the communication is interrupted temporarily. Furthermore, when the repetition frequency of UWS-EMP is high enough, the communication will be disrupted continually.

articleTitle: An improved Koch snowflake fractal broadband antenna for wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This study proposes a compact improved Koch snowflake fractal broadband planar antenna for the second generation (2G) to the fourth generation (4G), WLAN and navigation wireless applications. The device is based on the principles and structural features of conventional Koch fractal monopole antenna elements, combined with the advantages of trapezoid CPW-fed structure. The proposed antenna adapted two iterations Koch snowflake fractal structure radiator with one iteration Koch snowflake fractal slot inside, which covers more than ten mobile applications with a bandwidth of 106.25% (1.5-4.9GHz) for GPS, BDS, GLONSS, GALILEO, DCS1800, TD-SCDMA, WCDMA, CDMA2000, LTE33-41/42/43, Bluetooth, WLAN and WiMAX frequency bands. The proposed antenna was fabricated on a G10/FR4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.4 and a size of 72*42*1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The measurement results reveal that the omni-directional radiation patterns achieve a gain of -1.7-2.35dBi and an efficiency of 31-64%. The good agreement between the measurement results and simulation validates the proposed design approach and satisfies the requirements for various wireless applications.

articleTitle: Characteristic analysis and modeling for the near field radiation of FPGA
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: To predict the radiation emission of the FPGA, the radiation emission model for the chip is proposed with ICEM and the simulation result is also presented in this paper. The linear near-field surface scan system (LNFS) following electromagnetic compatibility standard is applied to measure the emission. It is illustrated that the simulation results agree with the measurements, so the value of the model for practical application is verified.

articleTitle: Stacked tri-band microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Shared aperture multiband antenna has more application when the electromagnetic compatibility problem is more and more serious. This paper proposes a novel stacked tri-band antenna which has three independent ports. Many dual band compact microstrip patch antenna has been designed but the research about tri-band microstrip antenna which can work in L, S and C band was little. To obtain tri-band operation, a stacked four layers of microstrip antenna working at different frequency is presented. Each of them is fed by dual feed probes. The simulated results show that the antenna can work at L band 1.66GHz, S band 3.25GHz and C band 5.27GHz with high isolation. The proposed antenna has achieved a bandwidth of 3%, 3% and 18% at each band, respectively.

articleTitle: Algorithm and implementation of radio frequency fingerprinting based on multi-resolution analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Wireless device accessing security is a great challenge in wireless communication networks, especially RFID and some other mini wireless terminals with limited computing power are facing higher strength security challenges because of the high cost caused by the traditional cryptographic. As an important non-cryptographic authentication technology, radio frequency fingerprinting technology, due to its full use of non-imitation of the radio frequency characteristics, has been gaining increasing attention to be a lightweight authentication scheme. Aiming at the shortcomings of traditional radio frequency fingerprint feature extracting methods, this paper constructs a system for the feature extraction of radio frequency fingerprint based on multi-resolution analysis. Meanwhile, BP neural network is designed to optimize features. Finally, a better separable metric algorithm and threshold value are selected according to the actual identification accuracy rate.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic leakage analysis based on arithmetic operation of FPGA
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The chips in working state have electromagnetic energy leakage problem. We offer a method to analyze the problem of electromagnetic leakage when the chip is running. We execute a sequence of addition and subtraction arithmetic instructions on FPGA chip, then we use the near-field probe to capture the chip leakage of electromagnetic signals. The electromagnetic signal is collected for analysis and processing, the parts of addition and subtraction are classified and identified by SVM. In this paper, for the problem of electromagnetic leakage, six sets of data were collected for analysis and processing. Good results were obtained by using this method.

articleTitle: Synthesis of unequally spaced array using multi-stage differential evolution algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Design of an unequally spaced linear array with pencil beam and low peak sidelobe level (PSLL) is very important to offer promising system capacity for wireless communication systems. However, most researchers have only focused on either the main beam width or the PSLL. In this paper, a multi-stage differential evolution algorithm (MSDEA) is proposed to jointly optimize the null-to-null beam width (NNBW) of the main beam, the PSLL and the power efficiency by designing a new objective function. Numerical results indicate that the proposed MSDEA algorithm outperforms the conventional DEA in terms of NNBW and power efficiency.

articleTitle: An experimental analysis of the effects of wiring harness during bulk current injection (BCI) test
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of ground return wires and crosstalk in wiring harness during BCI test are experimentally analyzed. The analysis shows that BCI coupling efficiency is significantly affected by the different wiring harness conditions such as wiring harness tightly bundled or wiring harness separated. Especially, during differential mode BCI test, the injected current can hardly be achieved unless all ground return wires, such as power ground and shielded layer, are routed outside the BCI probe.

articleTitle: Design of a simple structure OMT for millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this work we present a millimeter wave orthomode transducer (OMT) based on a simple structure. The OMT, with a square waveguide input (5.69 × 5.69 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and two single-mode waveguide outputs: a standard WR 22 waveguide (5.69×2.845 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), has no iris, no pins and no coupling structure. From 34 to 40.5 GHz the measured transmission is ≈-2 dB, the reflection coefficient of each port is less than -10 dB, the cross polarization is less than -29 dB for both polarizations. Analysis in this article will bring some methods to improve the OMT performance based on our structure.

articleTitle: A novel compact dual-mode filtering antenna for WiMax applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A novel compact filtering antenna is presented in 3.5GHz WiMax band. The filter-antenna is composed of a monopole antenna and a dual mode filter with shorted stub. The dual mode resonator works together with the coupling of capacitive source and load to form two transmission zeroes so that the filter has steep skirt selectivity and harmonic suppression. Further simulations and tests of the filtering antenna were carried out. Measured results show good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: Research on detection method for spatial discharge of high voltage electrical equipment based on ultraviolet monitoring video
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) imaging technology has the characteristics of strong anti-interference ability, high sensitivity and small size, leading to a broad application prospect in corona and partial discharge detection. However, the ultraviolet image analyzing technology nowadays is always affected by external environment and interference, which cause extra errors. Therefore, the ultraviolet image analyzing method needs further improvement. In this article, an effective detection method for the ultraviolet images of space discharge sources was studied. A noise reduction algorithm for ultraviolet images was designed, together with an identification and automatic extraction algorithm for deviant areas. The locating of discharge sources and the calculation of discharge distribution were achieved successfully on the platform in the laboratory, which validated the theoretical algorithm. The discharge characteristics were analyzed statistically, and the technical needs for the ultraviolet measuring platform and analyzing system were summarized. As a conclusion, an evaluation method for ultraviolet images was obtained.

articleTitle: A novel magneto-electric dipole antenna with wide H-plane triple-linear polarization and frequency reconfiguration for 5G application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A novel magneto-electric dipole antenna with wide H-Plane, triple-linear polarization and frequency-reconfiguration is proposed for 5G application. In this paper, the radiated dipoles are designed with the arc-shaped planes to exhibit wide H-plane performance. A bent cross-dipole with PIN diodes and varactor diodes inserted into its four arms is utilized to excite and control the antenna. Consequently, a wide H-plane ranging from -80 to 80 degrees can be achieved for 5G application. In addition, by controlling the PIN diodes and varactor diodes, the three kinds of linear polarizations and frequency reconfiguration functionalities for 3G/4G/5G applications can also be obtained.

articleTitle: A tri-band bandpass filter with wide stop band based on quad-mode stub loaded resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This paper presents a tri-band bandpass filter with high design flexibility in symmetrical structure and a wide stopband by using quad-mode stub loaded resonator. Stub-to-stub coupling is introduced to split two identical modes and produce two transmission zeros. The harmonic passband can be typically eliminated by regularly embedding open-circuited stubs in the feeding structure without affecting the performance of the three passbands. A filter prototype is simulated to validate the proposed design. The results show a desired wide upper stopband at 8.8 GHz with rejection better than 20 dB and three passbands are centered at 2.45 GHz, 3.68 GHz, and 5.19 GHz respectively, which is applicable to WLAN and WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: Analytical formulation for the coupling coefficient of equivalent impedance to calculated shielding effectiveness by TLM
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Based on Equivalent transmission line method, the coupling coefficient of apertures' equivalent impedance is required to calculate the shielding effectiveness of enclosures with apertures. According to the research results presently, the calculation method of coupling coefficient proposed presently could only been applied to that the E-field component existed in the orientation of apertures' narrowband it is lack of physical bas is to utilize the coupling coefficient to calculate the equivalent impedance of apertures. Contra posed to the above problems, a new analytical expression of coupling coefficient was derived with the method of mode matching. The contact among the coupling coefficient and equivalent impedance was established Further, the coupling coefficient could be used to calculate the shielding effectiveness of enclosures when the influence of high-order mode occurred By the coupling coefficient, We calculated the example of Po'ad[2], The correctness of the coupling coefficient is demons trated.

articleTitle: Analysis of soil resistivity characteristics under meteorological conditions in Haikou City
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Analysis of soil resistivity in Haikou City for nearly one year, the soil moisture data, and the meteorological data information provided by automatic meteorological station, the results show that soil resistivity of Haikou shows the distribution features of the east side lower than the west; soil resistivity of volcanic ash soil changes in inverse u-shaped curve with the seasons, while the red soil and sand soil resistivity changes with the seasons in u-shaped curve, and soil resistivity of the volcanic ash is not reduced due to the rainy season, instead it increases; soil resistivity of volcanic ash rises with the increase of soil humidity, while the soil resistivity of red soil and sand soil decreases with the increase of soil humidity. The soil resistivity of volcanic ash and red soil decreases with the increase of soil temperature, while the soil resistivity of sand soil rises with the increase of soil temperature. The soil resistivity of volcanic ash and red soil rises with precipitation, while soil resistivity of sand and red soil rises with precipitation. The decline of red soil was most pronounced.

articleTitle: Lightning localization using two MDF stations
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, we have established a magnetic direction finding (MDF) system with two MDF stations to reconstruct the position of the return striking point of cloud-to-ground lightning flashes. Numerical simulations are conducted to understand the possible mean squared errors (MSE) associated in calculating the potential striking point of lightning events with respect to the placement of the stations. It is shown that the location accuracy with two stations is heavily dependent on the orientation of the striking points. At the same angle estimation error level, the MSE for the areas in the vicinity of the line joining the two stations is larger than any other areas. Finally, the application of the MDF system in locating two cloud-to-ground flashes is presented. Comparing to the location results supplied by Jiangsu provincial Lightning Protection Center (LPC), the locations obtained by the MDF system are observed to be within a few hundreds of meters of LPS's. And the differences between the built MDF system and LPC turn out to be consistent with the simulation results in this paper.

articleTitle: Research on terahertz photoconductive antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A simulation analysis of the photoconductive antenna method was found. In this method, first the photocurrent of the antenna can be computationally investigated by a multi-physics model. Then, the full-wave electromagnetic solver is utilized to characterize the detected signal of the antenna. Finally, the terahertz generation characteristics are comprehensive studied by varying the geometrical parameters. Preliminary results is validated by previously reported observations, this approach can help to more effectively predict antenna performance.

articleTitle: Method for on-line detection of leakage current of power supply SPD
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: On-line detection of leakage current of Zinc oxide power supply SPD can be affected by many factors, such as harmonic voltage, inter-phase interference, etc. These factors mutually affect each other, making the problem quite complicated. How to eliminate the influence of inter-phase interference and voltage harmonic wave of system on MOV leakage current detection and thus improve the accuracy of results has always been the focus of attention. In this paper, we detected the phase difference between working voltage and total leakage current instead of detecting resistive leakage current. In addition, data fusion method that combined arithmetic mean and batch estimate was used to process on-line detection data of MOV. By using this method, the results can more accurately reflect the degradation of MOV.

articleTitle: Effects of potential difference within large grounding grid on secondary cables due to lightning strike
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: When substations suffer from lightning, the potential difference occurs within the grounding grid, which will generate induced voltage between the core, shield and the armor of the two-end grounded cables and significantly affect the secondary system in substation. This paper analyses the potential difference within large grounding grid and its influence on the secondary cables through the field test. The induced voltage in cable was measured and analyzed. The usage of drain wires was studied.

articleTitle: Analysis of wiring in the radiated disturbance measurement of electronic equipment
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The article illustrates that the wiring method has non-negligible impact on the radiated disturbance measurement of electronic equipment. The influence of wiring pattern has been analyzed during the measurement of radiated emission based upon the different laying manner of video wire, audio wire, keyboard wire, mouse wire and universal serial bus wire. Furthermore, the effect has been evaluated under such different cable arrangement in the radiated emission test. The research result shows the standardization arrangement of wiring has an important influence on the radiated disturbance measurement and result judgment, especially in the lower frequency range. The research result is meaningful and persuasive to the radiated disturbance measurement of electronic equipment in a correct and standardized way.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of spark-resistance formulae for micro-gap ESD in parallel disc electrodes
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Micro-gap electrostatic discharge (ESD) events due to a charged human body cause serious malfunction in high-tech information devices. For clarifying the mechanism, it is indispensable to grasp the spark properties of micro-gap ESDs. For this reason, two types of spark-resistance formulae proposed by Rompe-Weizel and Toepler have often been used so far to explain the spark process, however, the verification and applicability of these formulae still remain unknown. We previously measured spark currents from a human volunteer with charge voltages of 200 V or 2000 V in order to investigate which spark-resistance formula can explain the spark process. The result showed that the behavior of sparks from 200 V and 2000 V charged human can well be represented by the Toepler's and Rompe-Weizel's formulae, respectively. In this study, a new measurement setup for spark currents, which are difficult to be directly measured due to the charge neutralization through the spark channel, was developed by using parallel disc electrodes. The setup allows to simply estimating the spark current and the corresponding spark voltage from the measured discharge currents. From this setup, we confirmed that spark currents are almost identical to discharge currents from the disc electrodes with charge voltages of 500 V and 4000 V, to reveal that the Toepler's and Rompe-Weizel's formulae are applicable to predict the dynamic behavior of micro-gap sparks at charge voltages of 500 V and 4000 V, respectively, despite the fact that the spark lengths obtained from the most commonly used spark constants do not agree with the measured spark lengths. This finding supports our previous study.

articleTitle: Crosstalk-based radiated susceptibility test enforcing worst-case conditions and quantified overtesting margin
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A test setup based on crosstalk (XT) is designed to stress the equipment under test (EUT) with similar levels of interference as those in conventional radiated-susceptibility (RS) tests. Transmission-line theory is used to model both XT and RS test setups, and derive deterministic conditions of equivalence. At first, the forward power of the RF source (used to feed the XT test setup) is expressed in terms of known geometrical/electrical parameters of the test setup, including the impedance of the auxiliary equipment (AE) connected at the cable terminal opposite the EUT. Then, this quantity (generally unknown to test operators) is treated as a random variable, and statistical equivalent conditions for the XT-based test are derived. In particular, the proposed forward-power level ensures execution of a worst-case XT test which is more severe than the RS test in any case. The excess of injected interference is characterized through cumulative distribution functions.

articleTitle: Study of the radiated susceptibility of an electronic system using induced electromagnetic non-linear effects
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to propose an improved approach based on a novel non-intrusive method for easily assess the high frequency CW EM radiated susceptibility of an electronic system by characterizing its non-linear electromagnetic-effects. For this purpose, we have developed a specific harmonic frequency detection system coupled with a mode stirrer reverberating chamber. We describe the principles of the method, and we study a generic device board which is representative of a real electronic system. We evaluate the EM susceptibility of a micro controller in full functional mode and the data exchanges with two types of external 8Mb SRAM memories. We observe the EM radiated susceptibility of this device by a functional EMC analysis method; then we measure the harmonic frequency content and make a correlation with the EM susceptibility results. We obtain significant differences between the two memory devices, as a consequence of their different management of internal voltage over stress. We are well aware that this method is currently not validated in industrial environments EMC. In this paper, we only wanted to show that the appearance of the highest harmonic level occurs only when that DUT has the highest functional failure.

articleTitle: Practical implementation of metamaterials in a reverberation chamber to reduce the LUF
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Metamaterials have previously been shown to be a good solution to lower the LUF of reverberation chambers while conserving the required statistical field properties in terms of homogeneity, isotropy and random field polarization. In this paper, we propose to further explore the experimental implementation issues involved if one is to implement metamaterial in a reverberation chamber. The metamaterials previously used for numerical studies were based on metallic patches printed on a dielectric substrate of permittivity of 10; this makes experimental implementations on large surfaces costly and unattractive. A design methodology for metamaterials proposing identical electromagnetic properties along with a low-cost and easy to implement solution will be discussed. The results of their implementation on a reverberation chamber in terms of LUF will finally be shown.

articleTitle: A broadband Doherty power amplifier with modified post-matching structure
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, a novel broadband Doherty power amplifier (DPA) with an 800 MHz (42% fractional) bandwidth is presented. The modified post-matching structure and stepped transmission-line impedance transformation network are employed in the proposed design. As presented in this paper, an additional triple transmission line integrated in the output matching network of the peaking amplifier is regarded as output combiner and offset line. A novel Doherty power amplifier was designed by a packaged GaN HEMT to achieve the broadband characteristics. The measured results show that, the realized DPA exhibits 50%-60% drain efficiency (DE) at 6.5-7.5 dB power back-off and the maximum output power ranges from 43.5 to 45 dBm over the frequency band of 1.5-2.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Investigation and evaluations on new features for NR channel
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In order to meet the very challenging requirement of the next generation wireless communications, utilizing the very rich spectrum at high frequency band is very attractive. There are a lot of studies focusing on the millimeter wave communications in academia and industry. In the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> generation partnership project (3GPP), for studying the performance of the new radio (NR) systems operating at frequency bands above 6 GHz, a new accurate channel model is needed for these bands. Many research organizations made channel measurements in different locations all over the world and discovered several new features which are different from those in the current channel models below 6 GHz, such as blockage and oxygen absorption. Meanwhile, larger propagation loss will be encountered due to the higher frequency. Since the wavelength in high frequency bands is much smaller than that in low frequency bands, large antenna array is feasible. And by beamforming, it is possible to compensate the propagation loss. Beamforming can be applied at both transmitter and receiver sides. The highly directional links result in sharp beams at both sides. Necessary processing is needed to align the TX and RX beams and maintain it, e.g., via beam tracking. Due to these new observations, new features were developed in the high frequency channel model. In this paper, we review the new channel model, investigate its new features in system-level and show the impact of these new features on NR system design.

articleTitle: Lightning indirect effects on UH-1H helicopter: Numerical simulation analysis and EM shielding
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Lightning strike is a kind of threaten to the flying helicopter. The electromagnetic (EM) field, produced by the lightning attack, induces over voltage and current on the onboard cable bundles which result in disturbing or damaging of the sophisticated electronic and electrical equipment and seriously imperil flight safety. To obtain the distribution of internal magnetic field, we set an imitative UH-1H 3D model to conduct a simulation of impulse current injection in this paper. According to the simulation results, we establish a simple model of a new shielding material called BLW to get material property of the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness by means of the plane wave irradiation method. Besides, the material is used for the windshield in the entire helicopter model to simulate the comprehensive shielding effectiveness.

articleTitle: SPICE models of shielded twisted-wire pairs for radiated immunity analyses
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, SPICE models suitable to analyze the radiated immunity of shielded twisted-wire pairs (TWPs) are proposed. The equivalent circuits representation of shielded TWPs are firstly derived from the multiconductor transmission line (MTL) theory. Then, by the method of vector fitting (VF), the equivalent circuits are approximated by rational functions, which can be directly converted to SPICE models. The models are suitable for transient analyses and allows the incorporation of any kind of terminations (including non-linear or time-varying loads). Numerical results of port voltages induced on a shielded TWP induced by incident plane wave are presented and compared with other approaches.

articleTitle: Preliminary experimental validation of arrival direction detection system with two antennas for partial discharge noise
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: For secure power transmission and reliable power distribution, it is necessary to detect power equipment failure immediately when it occurs. In order to properly accomplish the failure detection, we pay attention to the measurement of a partial discharge noise at the electrical power equipment because the partial discharge should be observed before the failure due to insulation deterioration. In this paper, we developed an arrival direction detection system with a two antennas for the partial discharge noise. In the developed system, the two-dimensional angle of arrival (AOA) of the partial discharge noise was estimated based on the phase difference between two received signals. We experimentally evaluated the accuracy of the AOA detection in two types of situations: anechoic chamber and outdoor environment, for an amplitude modulated signal as the first step to simulate a partial noise. The experimental results demonstrated that the detection error of AOA was below 10 degrees.

articleTitle: Low-profile circularly polarized Fabry-Perot resonator antenna array with substrate integrated waveguide feed network
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A 2*2 low-profile circularly polarized Fabry-Perot resonator antenna array with a low cost substrate integrated waveguide feed network is presented. Patch squares are introduced on antenna ground as artificial magnetic conductor to resize the total antenna height to a quarter wavelength. The substrate integrated waveguide feed network are deliberately designed to produce a 90° phase difference at four output ports as to create sequential excitations for enhancement of antenna array circularly polarization performance. Whole antenna array structure is validated by HFSS with a gain of 16.5dBi at 5.8GHz and good circular polarization is obtained.

articleTitle: Effect of corrosion on the EMC characteristics of cable connector assembly
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Transfer impedance is an important parameter to represent the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of cable connector assembly. In this paper, the cable connector assemblies with different degradation degrees are obtained based on the accelerated corrosion test. The transfer impedances of these assemblies are measured using triaxial method. Based on the experimental results, an equivalent circuit model of degraded assembly's outer conductor and inner conductor under the environment of electromagnetic interference is developed. The relation between electromagnetic interference (EMI) current response coupling on the inner conductor and impedance of inner conductor is obtained and verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Combined FEM-reaction method for EMS analysis of a PCB in a low-Q enclosure
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, a combined method based on the finite element method (FEM) and the reaction theorem, is proposed to analyze the electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) of a printed circuit board (PCB) in a low-quality(Q) shielding enclosure. Here, we focus on the situation that an external incident electromagnetic interference (EMI) enters into an enclosure through aperture coupling, and further couples to the PCB inside the enclosure through board-edge coupling. The proposed method consists of three steps. Firstly, the incident fields inside the enclosure with the absence of the PCB are calculated by using the FEM. Then, the radiated fields of the PCB in the free space are also calculated by the FEM. Finally, the noise voltages on the PCB inside the enclosure due to the illumination of the EMI are calculated by using the incident fields and the radiated fields based on the reaction theorem. A direct method using the FEM is employed to validate the proposed method, and good agreement between the results obtained by the two methods is observed.

articleTitle: SPICE modeling of wideband RF front-end for electromagnetic coupling analyses
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This paper presents a SPICE model for the fast calculation of the coupling voltages of a wideband RF front-end illuminated by electromagnetic pulses with different parameters. A SPICE model of a wideband antenna for receiving based on Thevetin's theorem and the reciprocity theory is firstly established, which allows the incorporation of nonlinear loads. As a result, the SPICE model of the wideband RF front-end can be established by connecting a wideband LNA's SPICE model to the antenna SPICE model. The proposed SPICE model can be applied to both frequency-domain and time-domain analyses and can be used for nonlinear simulation. The SPICE model of a wideband RF front-end with frequency bands ranging from 0.8~20GHz, which is composed of an Archimedean spiral antenna and a low-noise travelling wave amplifier (TWA), is established and analyzed.

articleTitle: A novel wideband monopole antenna loading parasitical patches
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A novel wideband monopole antenna employing parasitical patches is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a microstrip-fed monopole antenna and two parasitical patches. In this paper, we utilize a stepped microstrip-fed structure to improve the impedance matching of the antenna to achieve a wide bandwidth. Furthermore, loading the parasitic patches can significantly improve broadband characteristics. A prototype antenna is manufactured using TLF-35A substrate. The measured bandwidth of the antenna goes from 2.66 GHz up to 5.48 GHz (69.3%) and has a peak gain of 2.15 dBi.

articleTitle: Two approaches for determining the whole-body average SAR in a reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: This paper aims to perform a comparison study of two approaches, two-step hybrid method and S-parameter measurement method, for determining the whole-body average-specific absorption rate (WBA-SAR) for rats in a reverberation chamber (RC). The two-step hybrid method incorporates finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) numerical solutions with electric field measurements in a RC-type exposure system; S-parameter measurement method is a totally experimental evaluation method to estimate the WBA-SAR in an RC. We first compare the WBA-SAR results derived in two rat-equivalent phantoms, then investigate the influence of measurement error on the relative error of WBA-SAR to clarify the validity and accuracy of these two approaches.

articleTitle: PCB layout modification to change the noise transfer path
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: To meet EN55015 regulation, the magnetic field distribution of 20W LED driver was tested by near field probes and spectrum analyzer. According to the tested magnetic strength, the interference sources and transfer paths on the PCB board were identified. Because the interference source cannot be changed, the PCB modification scheme was proposed to change the transfer path for the interference suppression. With the updated PCB layout, the conductive emission test result was dramatically improved to meet EN55015 regulation limit.

articleTitle: Non-contact measuring method for high-frequency impedance of load at the end of wire harness
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: Request to non-contact measurement method of load impedance connected to a wire harness is increasing rapidly. A method using network analyzer together with two current probes were previously proposed for this purpose, but it is valid only to 30 MHz. In this study, we extended the above-mentioned non-contact measurement method to 100 MHz by applying transmission line theory to the wire harness. The validity of the newly proposed measurement method was confirmed experimentally, and as a result the load impedance was measured with an error within 10% up to 100 MHz.

articleTitle: A compact and wideband circularly polarized slot antenna based on AMC for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The design of a compact and wideband circular polarization slot antenna using artificial magnetic conductors for satellite communication is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a square-loop slot, a feeding network, and an AMC surface. The feeding network is composed of a Wilkinson power divider, a 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>-phase shifter, and two straight feeding lines. The AMC surface is added at the backside of the slot antenna to enhance the boresight gains. Simulated and measured results including S11, axial-ratio (AR), radiation patterns, and realized boresight gains are given. The antenna can operate in the bandwidth of 4.65–6.15 GHz with left-handed circular polarization.

articleTitle: Study of an alternative method of indirect ESD test using folded-rhombic dipole-antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: We focused on the problems of the indirect discharge specified in IEC 61000-4-2. In the standard, it is regulated that an equipment under test (EUT) shall be set 10cm apart from a vertical coupling plane (VCP). However, there is no information what kind of electromagnetic field is emitted from the VCP when the indirect-discharge test specified in the standard. Therefore, we considered how electromagnetic field strength changed with a separation distance between the VCP and an EUT increasing. In the consideration, we used a shielded loop-antenna for a measurement of magnetic fields emitted from the VCP. Moreover, we examined an alternative test method of the indirect discharge using a folded-rhombic dipole-antenna, which is a radiator instead of the VCP. As a result, decrement of the field strength for the separation distance was not steep in a case where the folded-rhombic dipole-antenna is used as the radiator comparing the case of VCP. This result shows the antenna has a possibility to be used as the radiator of the indirect-discharge test instead of using VCP.

articleTitle: A new method to measure the dielectric constant in complex electromagnetic environment with black-box modeling regression method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, a novel black-box modeling multiband regression(BMMR) approach is presented for measuring the dielectric constant, overcoming the difficulty of measuring the dielectric constant in complex real environment with existing methods. In this approach, a simplified model based on black-box theory is built to obtain the field strengths within a certain frequency range of different dielectric constants. And a one-to-one mapping relation between dielectric constant and field intensity of the material to be measured in a certain frequency band is established by curve fitting. The dielectric constant of the material could be got through nonlinear regression equation of the standard curve by KNN (k-nearest neighbors) if its field strength is determined. Experimental results show that the BMMR methodology can calculate the dielectric constant accurately, which is especially appropriate for measuring the dielectric constant in a complex electromagnetic environment. In addition, BMMR make it possible to measure the dielectric constant by scanning.

articleTitle: A compact low-profile smartwatch antenna for wireless body local network application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A compact low-profile smartwatch antenna for wireless body area network (WBAN) application is introduced in this paper. Dual-band operating characteristic centered at 2.4GHz and 5.8GHz bands for ISM application could been realized by adopting feeding stub and coupling stub. Moreover, impedance matching and radiation efficiency are compared when the smartwatch antenna is placed in free space and mounted on wrist tissue model. The radiation efficiency is better than 35.0% in lower band and better than 38.5% in upper band when the smartwatch antenna is mounted on wrist tissue model with the distance of 6mm.

articleTitle: Analysis of lightning electromagnetic fields with metal layer surrounding the lightning rod system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, we set a metal layer to surround the lightning rod system to reduce the lightning electromagnetic fields when lightning strokes to the lightning rod All the underground fields amplitude decrease with the metal layer existing. Three influence factors are considered including metal layer height and grounding depth and distance between metal layer and lightning channel. The effect of metal layer height on underground electromagnetic fields is more notable than two other factors and mainly for electric fields. The metal layer grounding depth only affects the vertical electric field amplitude for the time more than 2 μs. The distance between metal layer and lightning channel can affect the vertical electric field slightly and hardly on two other kinds of fields. The horizontal electric field underground appears to be little affected by the metal layer. For comparison, we also discuss the effect of metal layer on the field aboveground and the results show that the reducing effect of metal layer on the fields aboveground is a little more obvious than that on underground fields.

articleTitle: Analysis on E-field environment inside the communication satellite
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: The analysis and calculation on the most severe electromagnetic environment inside the satellite, by calculating the E-field contribution of the transmit antennae through the structural panels of the satellite, and calculating the contribution of the passive link output section units (waveguide flanges, switches etc.) are given in this paper. The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) specification of the satellite could be edited according to this analysis. The results can also offer a reference during the process when the EMC control plan is carried out.

articleTitle: Analysis of radiation characteristics of multi-arm helix antenna using theory of circular array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
abstract: A very popular method to analyze the quadrifilar helix antenna is by equalizing it into two mutually perpendicular dipoles and two mutually perpendicular magnetic dipoles. In most of the available literature analyzing the quadrifilar helix antenna by using circular array theory has not been reported. In this paper quadrifilar helix antenna is equivalent to a circular array antenna which is consisted of four helix antennas along the ring. By this method the radiation pattern and polarization of helix, bifilar helix, trifilar helix and five-arm helix antenna are proposed and researched. When the number of the arm of multi-arm helix antennas is more than two, the radiation patterns are similar, they have a wide beam, wide 3 dB axial ratio radiation pattern on the meridian plane and omnidirectional radiation pattern on the equatorial plane. And a trifialr helix antenna is modeled and simulated. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna exhibits the gain of 5.8 dB in the maximum radiation direction, half power beamwidth of 2θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">05</sub> =120°, 3 dB axial ratio of θ = 155° on the meridian plane, and omnidirectional radiation pattern on the equatorial plane, and the reflection coefficient |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>| <;-10dB over the frequency band from 1.505 to 1.627 GHz.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of electromagnetic emissions for broadband power line (BPL) communication
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE 5th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC-Beijing)
